body.p: Remarks

As stated above, Applicant appreciates the Examiner's thorough examination of the subject application and requests reexamination and reconsideration of the subject application in view of the preceding amendments and the following remarks.

As of the subject action, claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 were pending in the subject application, of which claims 1, 19, and 27 are independent claims. With this Response, Applicant has amended claims 1, 19, and 27. Applicant respectfully submits that no new matter is believed to have been entered as a result of this Response. All objections and rejections are respectfully traversed.

Applicant and the undersigned Attorney would like to thank Examiner Joyce for allowing the Applicant Initiated Interview on September 19, 2023 and for contributing to advance this Application closer to allowance. Generally, as will be elaborated upon in greater detail below, the issue discussed involved the amendments made herein.

While during the interview Examiner Joyce was understood to initially agree that the claims as discussed overcome the cited prior art, it was noted that the cited prior art may be reviewed to verify Applicant's contentions and that another search may be conducted. If a new search results in new art, Applicant respectfully requests that the undersigned Attorney be contacted to discuss the art before issuing the next Office Action. Examiner Joyce is encouraged to contact the undersigned Attorney with any questions or suggestions for Examiner's Amendment.

Applicant has amended the specification by adding paragraph [0037] based on the first paragraph of page 6 of U.S. U.S. Provisional Application upon which the subject application claims priority. As such, Applicant respectfully submits that newly added paragraph [0037] does not recite new matter under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).
Drawings

The drawings were objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a) for not showing the "second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem" in claims 1, 19, and 27. Without conceding the objection, Applicant has cancelled this feature from claims 1, 19, and 27. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that this objection be withdrawn.

Claims 1-6, 12-16, 19-23, and 27-30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being anticipated by Tian et al. (U.S. Patent No. 10,065,314, hereinafter referred to as "Tian") in view of Edinger et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,346,160, hereinafter referred to as "Edinger"). Claims 8-11 and 24-26 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Tian in view of Edinger, and further in view of Gilbertson et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,827,678, hereinafter referred to as "Gilbertson"). Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Without conceding the rejection and in an effort to accelerate prosecution of the subject application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 19, and 27. Representative
independent claim 1 is recited below for convenience:
1. (Currently Amended) A detachable, self-contained robotic arm
system comprising:
a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous
mobile base;
a slew ring coupled to the mounting subsystem; a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem

a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the slew ring mounting subsystem, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm
system;

p.del: a second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem,
herein the second machine vision system is configured to

body.p: enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm subsystem; a control subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem and configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem;
and
a connectivity subsystem configured to detachably couple the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system to one or more external
systems.
Support for these amendments may be found in at least FIGS. 1-2 and newly amended paragraph [0037] of the subject application as filed, which are reproduced below for
convenience.
[0037] A slew ring is shown which serves as joint A for the arm. This provides a pivoting motion for the base of the arm relative to the robot and the control box.

Note that in this embodiment the motor powering the slew ring is placed above and along the main axis of the electronics control box and mounting bracket attached to the slew ring base which allows the vertical observation post, to pivot with the motion of the arm. This allows continuous observation of the arm and
payload and to avoid collision of the moving arm with the observation post.
(See, subject application, FIGS. 1-2 and paragraph [0037]).

Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Tian, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson fails to teach, disclose, or even suggest "a slew ring coupled to the mounting subsystem"; "a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative to the mounting subsystem"; and "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system."
For example, in rejecting independent claim 1, the subject action states "Tian teaches a robotic arm system comprising: a robotic arm subsystem (330) mounted on a platform (310)

which is an autonomous mobile base (340); a first machine vision subsystem (324) mounted on a mast assembly (320), wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm system; a second machine vision subsystem (334) mounted on the robotic arm subsystem, wherein the second machine vision system is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm subsystem; and a control subsystem (column 13, lines 30+) configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem." See, subject action, p. 3. FIG. 3 of Tian is reproduced below for convenience.
(See, Tian, FIG. 3).

As can be seen from at least the above-cited portions of Tian, the combination of Tian, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest a slew ring coupled to the mounting subsystem, a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, where the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative to the mounting subsystem; and a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the slew ring, where the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system. As such, Applicants respectfully submit that the combination of Tian and Edinger is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest Applicant's claimed "a slew ring coupled to the mounting subsystem"; "a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative to the mounting subsystem"; and "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self- contained robotic arm system."
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 under § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Tian, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson be withdrawn.

In this response, Applicant has amended various claims and/or asserted arguments in this application to facilitate expeditious prosecution of the application. Applicant is not conceding that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to the instant action, and/or having interpretations other than presented herein are unpatentable over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by any claims prior to this response, claims having different interpretations than presented in this response, and additional claims.

In consideration of the amendments and foregoing discussion, Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is in condition for allowance. While Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is now in condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to telephone Applicant's representative (617-854-1420) to facilitate prosecution of this application. Please apply any charges or credits to the above-noted deposit account.
Respectfully submitted,
